costScope: Full ordinary gift in donor numerator. All ten specialty allocations sum to one and include recipient program, management, fundraising and failed-referral work. Separate gross associated resource sensitivity includes all nominal services, not merely health-credited cases; no waived-charge multiplier. Prospective cash per-service costs are judgments anchored to 2025 recipient cash-like scale. Whole legal-recipient finance also includes disclosed fiscal sponsorship of Western Farm Workers Association; its amount is not separately established. We retain the full gift and whole-recipient spending calibration, add no unverified sponsorship health, and test a ten-percent loss of clinical activity. The sponsorship is not silently removed from costs. Gross associated resources include nominal activity even when a gift adds none and therefore are not net marginal social costs.
geographicAttribution: Current patient eligibility requires residence in Northern California or the Central Valley. Accordingly all modeled direct patient benefit is assigned to California: Q_CA=Q_all. This is a service-eligibility inference, not headquarters/population allocation; no Bay=0.6 or SF=0.08 factor is reused. Migration or secondary spillovers are unmodeled. Geographic nesting means these QALYs must not be summed with the same services' Bay/USA benefits.
formula: Let F(r,H)=(1-exp(-r*H))/r with F(0,H)=H. For specialty k: nominal S_k=C*a_k/c_k; S=sum S_k; activity A=min(S*f,K)/S. For disjoint diagnosis path j within k: P_j=S_k*s_j*A*d_j/r_j, where s=case share,d=nonoverlap fraction,r=services/person. Symptom Q_j=P_j*[success_j*utility_j*(1+discount)^(-delay_j)*F(catchup_j+loss_j+mortality_j+ln(1+discount),horizon_j)-harm_j]. For CRC let z(t)=delta_hazard*exp(-catchup*latency)*F(catchup,min(max(t-latency,0),active_years)); Δsurvival(t)=exp(-baseline_mortality*t)*(exp(z(t))-1). CRC Q=P_crc*[linkage*surviving_utility*(1+discount)^(-delay)*integral_0^H Δsurvival(t)*(1+discount)^(-t)dt - harm]. Sum CRC, cataract, hernia and all named symptom paths, subtract independent harm once. Q_CA=Q_all; donor_price_10=10*C/Q_CA for positive Q_CA. Full exact parameter vectors and scenario overrides are below. Numeric reproduction uses existing lib/oa-portfolio-model.mjs and lib/oa-portfolio-foundation.mjs; its regions.us.q equals CA here solely because eligibility was independently verified. The modeled service and patient equivalents represent completed care at the procedure date. The pre-procedure delay is discounted financially in time; no separate survival/catch-up attrition before completion is applied because it is assumed included in additional completed activity. If nominal activity instead means referrals, an additional completion/dropout factor is required. Procedural harm is conservatively charged without a favorable delay discount.
counterfactual: Without a new gift, existing funded OA care and other providers continue. f represents the fraction of nominal activity that is maintained/expanded because of new funds, K capacity; catch-up hazards separately represent patients obtaining equivalent care later. Modern medical management and spontaneous remission remain alternatives. Uninsured at intake does not mean no lifetime access. Current English eligibility says uninsured/ineligible for full-scope public coverage, while OA's March 2025 funder presentation describes bridge care for some people who may qualify. Actual current intake implementation remains unverified. Neither uninsured status nor grant loss establishes lifelong absence of care. Current coverage restrictions can increase need but do not quantify donor-sensitive appointments.
attribution: Within each specialty, diagnosis shares sum to one. Every modeled path uses r=1,529/1,130 and d=1: the aggregate unduplicated count already absorbs repeats/overlap, so no additional blanket patient discount is added. Applying one aggregate conversion uniformly to unknown diagnosis-specific and marginal activity is a judgment; the alpha conversion remains a sensitivity. This accounting partitions patient-equivalents without claiming actual unique-person linkage. Provider capacity and funding replacement enter f and K once; later equivalent care enters the separate catch-up hazard. There is no extra navigation multiplier on completed services, provider credit multiplier, productivity benefit, or duplicate all-cancer survival benefit.
uncertainty: Conditional scenario model dominated by diagnostic mix, baseline utility, funding additionality and later-care assumptions. Favorable, rapid-catch-up, null and adverse states are deliberately wide stress tests, not probability intervals or empirical bounds. The central input set is a transparent judgment, not an observed expectation. Twenty-one supplementary named paths plus CRC/cataract/hernia cover the full specialty allocation; the small other-assessment path has no central benefit and retains burden.
nativeOutcomes: 2025 Form 990 Part III reports 1,529 surgical/diagnostic services for 1,130 unduplicated residents: 1.353097 services per person. Specialty service counts sum to 1,529, but patient-linked diagnosis frequencies remain unavailable. Beta uses the observed aggregate ratio across all diagnosis paths as a judgment transfer to marginal activity, replacing the older repeat/overlap priors. The output is disjoint patient-equivalents, not 24 independently observed patient cohorts. The 2025 whole-recipient cash-like average is $1,476 per service, not a marginal quote. At the $100,000 gift normalization, the central has 66.727 nominal mixed services, 33.364 additional service equivalents and 24.657 patient equivalents. Gift cost is $2,997.27 per additional service and $4,055.60 per patient equivalent before diagnosis-specific utility, timing and harms. These are conditional marginal equivalents, not actual quoted slots or a new observed treatment cohort.

inputs.name: crc_active_years
inputs.rationale: Five years of possibly different fatal hazard after latency, not five avoided deaths or a life expectancy.

inputs.name: crc_horizon_years
inputs.rationale: Ten-year finite survival observation from procedure; both arms return to common mortality after the hazard-effect window. No lifetime tail.

sensitivity: Central 0.531150 California QALYs per $100,000, or $1,882,706 per ten QALYs. This is a conditional judgment, not measured OA effectiveness or a recommendation.

The observed aggregate patient conversion changes central health by only 3.40% from alpha; its diagnosis-specific transfer remains unknown. Reverting fully to alpha conversion reproduces 0.513674 QALYs.

Central nominal activity is 66.727 services; f=0.5 gives 33.364 additional service-equivalents and 24.657 disjoint patient-equivalents. The K=100 cap does not bind. Five available slots instead yields 0.079600 QALYs ($12.56M per ten); f=0.1 yields 0.106230 ($9.41M). Neither slot count is observed.

Supplementary pathways without relief yield -0.014544 QALYs; all gross benefits null yields -0.087362. Zero clinical activity gives zero; adding one independent QALY of harm gives -1. Negative or zero health has no favorable price.

Rapid later care yields 0.048612 QALYs ($20.57M per ten); favorable combined assumptions yield 2.212014 ($452,077). One-year symptom horizons give 0.297722, whereas limiting CRC as well gives 0.293068. CRC latency prevents survival gain before year two.

AUB contributes 0.125349 net QALYs, the largest single path. Setting only AUB relief to zero, retaining harm, lowers total to 0.379380. Its 65% gynecology share, 0.10 utility and 0.8 success are priors, not trial estimates in OA patients.

Gross associated resources are $369,105.29, giving $6.95M per ten California QALYs. This includes nominal clinical, patient and downstream costs; it is neither waived hospital charges nor net incremental societal spending.
At this donor margin, meeting $1M per ten QALYs requires 1 QALY per $100,000 (1.88 times central), and $100k requires 10 (18.83 times). These are arithmetic thresholds, not benchmark endorsements.
